## Connection 



The connection patterns in MPX NYC highlight a city alive with intimacy and community. Most participants maintained active networks of queer and trans friends—many with frequent contact both social and physical. Even in a moment defined by a health emergency, touch and togetherness remained central to queer life (see @tbl-connection). 

::: {.callout-note collapse=true icon=false}
# Show Table 6.2: Connection

{{< include tbl-connection.qmd >}}

:::

Roughly two-thirds of respondents reported contact with at least one queer or trans friend in the past month, while one in five maintained larger networks of ten or more.  

Travel patterns further emphasize the geography of connection: about one-third traveled 16–30 minutes for hookups, another third more than 30 minutes, mapping a social city whose bonds stretch across boroughs.  
 
Perhaps most striking, nearly 40 percent of participants had sexual or physical contact with multiple people at once —- a reminder that group settings were not fringe, but part of the normal social life through which health messages and interventions must travel.
